game: Carolina Panthers at Green Bay Packers, Week 8 2026, kickoff time not in pack, Lambeau Field outdoor, spread GB -3.5, total 47, implied totals GB 25.2 and CAR 21.8, moneyline not saved, weather not saved

script.base: Green Bay is a short home favorite (GB -3.5, total 47, implied GB 25.2 / Carolina 21.8), so the base script is a one-score game with GB ahead late, not a blowout and not a shootout. Carolina is exactly a +3.5 dog, which is the threshold where the dog throws a bit more, but Chuba Hubbard still enters with the carry monopoly (55 of 70 Carolina rushes, 275 yards in weeks 4/6/7) until the score forces them off it. Carolina's two guards are out (Damien Lewis, Torricelli Simpkins III) into a Green Bay blitz of 34% that has already cut Carolina to 0.00 EPA/dropback vs blitz against 0.16 with no blitz, so Bryce Young's throws should tilt shorter than Tetairoa McMillan's 290 air yards and Jalen Coker's 204 air yards. Green Bay's own run is a committee (Marshawn Lloyd 24/61, Pierre Strong 16/35, Josh Jacobs 11/36, K. Johnson 8/24 in weeks 5-7) and its pass game is vertical (Matthew Golden 477 air yards, Christian Watson 425) into a Carolina blitz of 37% that has Green Bay at -0.08 EPA/dropback vs blitz and +0.22 clean.
script.flip1: Green Bay jumps up by two scores early at Lambeau, runs the clock, and Carolina abandons Hubbard. Carolina air yards pile onto McMillan (31 targets in the three-game window) and Coker, Hubbard's rush line dies, and Green Bay starter volume stalls only if the lead gets out of a -3.5 game. This flip hits a Coker yards over and can squeeze John Metchie if the tree goes fully vertical.
script.flip2: Carolina's run game controls clock despite the guard losses, or Green Bay's center Sean Rhyan and guard Travis Glover being out plus Carolina's blitz turn it into a grind. Deep shots (Watson, Golden, Coker, McMillan) die, short targets (Metchie, Tommy Tremble, Tucker Kraft) and whoever actually gets Green Bay's late carries matter, and the 47 total comes under. Weather is not saved, so a Lambeau wind/rain version of this flip is unconfirmed.

injury_fallout: Source is the pack's official pre-game injury report, not 90-minute inactives. Carolina offense loses G Damien Lewis (knee, Out) and G Torricelli Simpkins III (ankle, Out): pressure up, Hubbard efficiency down, more quick throws, so deep yards for McMillan and Coker are the losers and short options (Metchie 12 targets / 91 air, Tremble 10/39 air, Hubbard 9 targets at -7 air) are the gainers. Carolina defense loses LB Jaelan Phillips (hamstring, Out) and CB Akayleb Evans (triceps, Out), with DT Bobby Brown III questionable (hand): Carolina's 6-game rates (5.31 rush YPC allowed, only 9 passes of 20+ for 211 yards, 37% blitz) overstate today's pressure and coverage, which helps Jordan Love's time and whoever replaces Evans. Green Bay loses LB Zaire Franklin (shin, Out): underneath/hook help for Carolina's TE, slot, and back receiving (Metchie, Tremble, Darren Waller, Hubbard catches). Green Bay also loses C Sean Rhyan (ankle, Out) and G Travis Glover (knee, Out), so Lloyd/Jacobs/Strong efficiency is down even against Carolina's bad run defense. Unresolved questionables: Matthew Golden (shoulder) can dump 32 targets onto Watson, Kraft, Savion Williams, and Bo Melton if he sits or is limited; DT Devonte Wyatt (ankle), DT Anthony Campbell (ankle), and LB Brenton Cox Jr. (quad) can soften Green Bay's 4.08 YPC run defense if they sit. No WR, RB, or TE is ruled Out.

Carolina blitzes 37% and Green Bay's EPA/dropback falls from 0.22 clean to -0.08 when blitzed, which is the same deep-shot problem for Golden and Watson, but Phillips being out means Carolina may not get home at that 37% rate.

Carolina bleeds the run (5.31 YPC, 22 runs of 10+) and the middle (7.93 YPA) and does not bleed 20+ passes (9 in 6 games). Evans out can open a corner spot those 6 games do not capture.
matchup.overlap: Carolina's primary target is Tetairoa McMillan (31 targets, 318 yards, 290 air yards in weeks 4/6/7). That downfield role does not overlap a Green Bay defense that is best on the right and blitzes 34%, and his 73 receiving line has no two-sided price. The overlap that is in the pack is the quick/intermediate tree: John Metchie 12 targets, 81 yards, 91 air (~7.6 aDOT) plus Franklin's LB absence. Jalen Coker is the opposite overlap: 17 targets, 106 yards, 204 air (~12 aDOT, 6.2 yards per target) into the blitz and the guard losses. Green Bay's primary pair, Golden (32/266/477, questionable shoulder) and Watson (24/264/425), does not overlap Carolina's bleed (middle and the run). Tucker Kraft (19/149/108) does overlap the middle and the blitz checkdown, but 46 has no two-sided price and his last four (42, 64, 37, 48) sit on the number.

Both blitz rates and the EPA splits (Carolina 0.00 vs blitz / 0.16 clean; Green Bay -0.08 vs blitz / 0.22 clean) point to pressure, short targets, and fading unconfirmed deep shots.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both legs lost. Metchie finished under 15.5 because, once Damien Lewis and Torricelli Simpkins could not hold the 34% Green Bay blitz, Bryce Young only looked vertical: Tetairoa McMillan (31 targets, 290 air yards in the window) and Jalen Coker took the tree, Metchie saw two targets on Green Bay's right side (5.66 YPA), and the -116 was just juice on a consensus coin-flip the market had already shaded for a role cut not in this pack. Coker went over 62.5 the way he already did at 97 and 66, one 40-yard play against a defense that has allowed 13 passes of 20+ in 7 games, and Carolina's +3.5 pass bump became the two-score chase in flip 1. That Coker counter is almost as strong as the pace read, which is why he is a lean and not a strong. Metchie's four-game floor of 19 still beats that counter inside this pack, so he stays, flagged for price and missing sims, not cut. No bet is placed.
slip_story: One script only: Carolina quick game under Green Bay pressure, not a shootout and not a Green Bay clock-kill stack. Metchie receiving over 15.5 and Coker receiving under 62.5 win together if the blitz and the two-guard loss turn air yards into checkdowns and incompletions. They lose together if Carolina trails big and only throws deep. Do not add a game-total under, a McMillan or Watson or Golden over, a Hubbard rush over into a 4.08 YPC defense, or any touchdown. Two legs, one market per player. Weather, final inactives, coverage charting, sims, and Pinnacle are all missing, so this is a flagged read for the human, not a wager.
